newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber closes lower but pares limit losses.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber closes lower but pares limit losses.

text.p: Late short covering pared early limit losses of $10.00 per tbf in September and November CME lumber futures with prices ending lower to sharply lower on continued pressure from a weak cash market, traders said.
Lumber closed $7.80 to $2.00 per tbf lower with September off $336.50 and November off most at $334.80 per tbf.

September posted a new contract low of $332.00 and November $332.60 when they fell the daily limit earlier on pressure from continued slow cash trade and a weak undertone to cash prices. Wood supplies are high at the mill level and are seen rising further on a seasonal basis, traders said.

"(Mills) are coming back from their curtailment period, their (summer) maintenance shutdowns, so production actually in another two or three weeks is going to be higher than it is right now," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.

Schmaedick noted that mills have a lot of wood on hand. They kept asking prices at fairly high levels which cut sales and now demand is slack. Even a strike would not effect supplies because inventories at the mills and reloads appear large enough to meet demand for a month or more, he added.
